messages:
mikaela: Quick sync — I want to propose a small change to the credential ownership model. Right now API keys can be 'project' or 'org' scoped but it's ambiguous who 'owns' long-lived service keys. Thoughts?

samir: +1 to clarifying ownership. We've hit edgecases where devs create keys in infra but product teams think they own them.

mikaela: Proposal sketch: add explicit owner metadata on every credential: owner_type: one of [user, project, org, service] and owner_id string. Keep existing scope fields but prefer owner metadata for decisioning.

june: How would that interact with runtime authz checks? e.g. route-level RBAC currently looks at scope and role.

mikaela: Runtime flow: if owner_type==service -> enforce service-level bindings (service RBAC). Else fallback to scope-based resolution (project then org). That avoids scanning for a logical owner by searching multiple tables.

lee: I'm worried about backfill and migration. We have millions of keys in the index. Adding owner metadata is cheap, but who sets it for legacy keys?

mikaela: Two-step: 1) for new keys set owner metadata at creation. 2) for legacy keys run an offline heuristic job to infer owner (creator, creation context, bucket). Mark inference with inferred_owner flag so UI shows it.

samir: What about ambiguous cases where a key is created using a project token but then used by infra pipelines? Owner should reflect intent not usage.

mikaela: Agreed — we should default owner to the entity that minted the key (creator principal). If team wants to reassign, provide an explicit transfer API that requires an approval flow.

june: Approval flow seems heavy. Could we allow owners to set a 'delegated_to' array of principals? Then runtime checks consider delegation chains with a TTL.

lee: Delegation is useful but opens audit complexity. We need to log delegation changes and support revocation. Also make sure performance doesn't degrade — we can't call out to a slow service per token auth.

mikaela: Implementation notes: store owner and delegation inline in the credential record. Keep a small fixed-size delegation list (max 8). Use a single-table lookup during authz. Revocations are just updates to the credential row — fast.

samir: How do RBAC roles map when owner_type==service vs owner_type==project? Example: a 'reader' role on org vs 'svc-ingest' role on service.

mikaela: We map role namespaces: service roles are evaluated against service role graph; project/org roles against resource RBAC. If a credential has both owner metadata and explicit role bindings, role bindings win. Otherwise infer role by owner namespace.

june: Edge case: borrowed keys — someone copies an org key into a project secret store. Owner remains org, but runtime is called from project. We should not silently widen permissions.

lee: Agreed. Runtime must always check owner bindings, not caller runtime location. Caller context still matters for request-level constraints (e.g., IP, VPC), but owner RBAC determines which resources can be accessed.

mikaela: Example credential payload (proposal):
```
{
  "key_id": "k_abc123",
  "owner_type": "org",
  "owner_id": "org_42",
  "inferred_owner": false,
  "delegated_to": ["project_7", "service_ingest"],
  "role_bindings": ["org:reader"]
}
```

samir: Looks good. We should also add 'created_by' and 'created_context' to help inference and for audit.

mikaela: Yes — created_by, created_from (UI/API/CLI), and created_at will be tracked.

june: Rollout plan? I'm thinking: feature flag for writing owner fields; set defaults for new keys; run inference job for legacy keys; slowly enable runtime strictness behind a flag; then flip enforcement globally after 2 weeks of metrics.

lee: Also add a mutation endpoint for transfer/delegation that requires either owner approval or a platform admin override. Put soft-locks for keys that are part of active Dedicated reservations.

mikaela: Good call — lock semantics for reserved infra keys.

infra-bot: deploy-check — flagged schema change to credentials table. Need migration plan: add columns owner_type, owner_id, inferred_owner boolean, delegated_to jsonb, role_bindings jsonb, created_context string. Estimated 2h downtime for full-table rewrite unless we use online migration.

lee: Use online add-column + backfill async to avoid downtime. We'll need an index on (owner_type, owner_id) for fast lookups.

mikaela: Decision checklist:
- add owner metadata for new keys behind feature flag (agree)
- run inference backfill and mark inferred_owner (agree)
- implement transfer API + audit log (agree)
- runtime enforcement gated by flag, monitor errors (agree)

samir: SGTM. I'll write a short RFC with the examples and rollout steps and link it here.

mikaela: Thanks — tagging @june and @lee for follow-ups on the transfer API and migration ops. :thumbsup:

june: I'll draft the API contract.

lee: I'll scope the migration and index work.

mikaela: Cool — meeting-free sync. If anyone objects, speak up in the next 24h.

samir: +1 :eyes:

infra-bot: rfc-create: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/credential-ownership-1776009999 (draft)
